extracted.intended_audience: university mathematics instructors, MOOC designers, and educational researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for designing and evaluating a skills-based MOOC aimed at lifting mathematics skills and scaffolding a wide range of learners, including those with high stress and low self-efficacy. Emphasises data-driven evaluation and integration with existing face-to-face supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: lift mathematics skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The MOOC was developed to lift maths skills at the university and in the community where maths skills continue to be a challenge and in some cases a source of stress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design course content and learning activities explicitly targeted at improving specific mathematical skills gaps for both enrolled students and community learners; measure outcomes against those targeted skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills-based MOOC design
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterise the course as a 'skills-based' MOOC rather than a purely content/lecture MOOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus learning design, assessments, and activities on practice and mastery of discrete skills; align modules to scaffolded skill development rather than broad theoretical coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complement existing face-to-face supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an alternative online way to support students who struggle with mathematics at university level, as a complement to the existing face to face small group workshops and individual consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate the MOOC with institutional support services (e.g., point learners to workshops and consultations); design tasks that reinforce or prepare learners for in-person help rather than replace it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaffolding to address affective factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Design scaffolding learning experiences to address high-stress and low self-efficacy in maths learners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include progressive supports (worked examples, guided practice, formative feedback, low-stakes assignments) and affective supports (encouraging messaging, incremental difficulty) specifically to reduce anxiety and build confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive design for a wide range of learners
rubrics_metrics.description: Scaffold a wide range of learners—the MOOC 'scaffolds wide range of learners'—to accommodate differing prior knowledge and confidence levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide multiple entry points, optional extension tasks, adaptive pathways or clearly signposted prerequisite refreshers to support both novices and more prepared learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and scheduling relative to academic terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Run the MOOC in the last four weeks of the summer holiday, prior to the Autumn session, as a preparatory offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider scheduling preparatory MOOCs immediately before formal teaching to maximise usefulness as remediation or readiness support for incoming or continuing students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use enrolment and demographic data for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyse enrolment numbers and participant demographics to understand reach, who the course serves, and equity of access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use analytics of student patterns of use
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sources include analytics data of student patterns of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor engagement metrics (time on task, video views, resource access patterns, progression through modules) to evaluate uptake, identify bottlenecks, and inform iterative design improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse assignment submission data
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sources include assignment submission data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine submission rates, scores, and common errors to assess learning gains, task difficulty, and where additional scaffolding or instructional clarification is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect qualitative learner feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Data sources include qualitative feedback via online forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use open-ended surveys, course reflections, and feedback forms to capture learner perceptions, affective responses, and suggestions; triangulate qualitative data with analytics and assessment outcomes for richer evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge non-binary MOOC models
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides support for recent non-binary definitions of MOOCs (Lane 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should recognise MOOCs exist along continuums (e.g., credit vs non-credit, skills vs content, solitary vs blended) and choose a model appropriate to the institution's aims and learners' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to discipline-specific design issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Discusses the importance of discipline specific issues in the design of the MOOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing MOOCs for mathematics, explicitly address domain-specific challenges (e.g., abstract reasoning, cumulative prerequisite knowledge, anxiety about maths) rather than applying generic MOOC templates.
